Rationale: the gate and cluster primitives live in `packages/services/service-cluster` (services-lane packages); the deliverable is a new operator-visible reading of the existing advisory verdict — a public-surface addition, hence Feature, already maintainer-authorized (ruled C on #8501, 2026-08-27). Serial constraints cleared: `service-cluster/**` free; no services-lane card in flight on it. Sibling dispatches this round are #12685 (`service-automation`) and #11993 (`plugin-approvals`) — disjoint packages, no read coupling.

## Ruled by the maintainer — ⛔ none of this is re-openable

Provenance on the card: maintainer ruling 2026-08-27, verbatim 「其他接受」, adopting **Option C** on #8501.

⇒ Settled: make a licensed `max_nodes` **oversell visible to operators**. The atomic slot-claim enforcement mechanism is **deliberately not built now**, deferred until real commercial pull.

⛔ Explicitly out, and this is the line the card will be judged on: **no enforcement, no membership view, no slot claim, no refusal behaviour.** The gate verdict is advisory and **stays** advisory — this card makes the advisory reading reach a human. Sub-decisions (TTL semantics, refusal posture) stay unmade until #8501's reopen triggers fire.

⚠️ The tempting overreach is specific: while wiring a display you will see how easy a real count would be. That is the card #8501 deliberately did not order. ⛔ Do not build toward it, and do not word the surface as though enforcement exists.

## Premise-first — the card names the three facts and the seam that moved

Re-measure all three on today's tree **before designing**; the seam changed at #8503:

- the gate is consulted **once per process at boot** (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`);
- there is **no cluster membership view** (`generateNodeId` is random per process);
- `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` is an **operator-declared count, identical in every replica** (`split-brain-guard.ts`).

⭐ Those three together are why this is visibility and not enforcement: nothing in the process knows how many peers actually exist. **Whatever you surface must not read as though it does.** "Declared replicas vs licensed cap" is an honest sentence; "N nodes running" is not, and would be a false statement dressed as telemetry.

Build on the verdict vocabulary #8367 / PR #8503 landed — `admitted` / `refused` / `capped` — rather than inventing a second vocabulary. #8504 already landed the serve-time loud warning; ⛔ do not duplicate it, extend the reach.

## Second premise, to settle early

The card's own instruction: **establish where the reading can actually land before writing it.** If the display half is a console surface in `objectui`, stop and report for cross-repo splitting. A telemetry-only landing inside this repo is a legitimate smaller answer — say so with the reading rather than reaching for the console.

## Verification

- `service-cluster` suite; a test that asserts **what an operator sees** for each verdict, not merely that a value was computed.
- ⚠️ Include the honest-wording assertion: pin that the surface does **not** claim observed membership. That is the regression most likely to arrive later as a "helpful" wording change.
- Gate union from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` on your **actual** changed set; exit codes before any pipe. `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is **NOT MEASURED**, not red — build and re-run, report both.
- **Ablation**: show the new surface goes red/absent when the verdict changes, on the specific rows.
- **Changeset**: argue it. ⛔ Never empty.
- ⛔ No model names in any pushed artifact.

## Report

Post your terminal JSON report as a comment on **this issue first**, then return it. Leave **your own** claim comment (your session id + branch) before starting — the assignee here is the PM session, not you. Include the measured answer to "where can the reading land" as a named field.

## PM review of record — **ACCEPT**

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`, round 3. PR #12720 @ `b7d45784`.

### ⭐ The cross-repo question was answered by measurement, and I verified it myself

The brief said to stop and report if the display half landed in `objectui`. It doesn't, and the reason is decisive rather than a judgement call. Checked independently on `origin/main`, not taken from the report:

- `packages/console/package.json` → `exports: { "./package.json": "./package.json" }`, `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`;
- **zero tracked `.ts`/`.tsx` files** under `packages/console` — 4 tracked files in total.

⇒ There is no console source in this repo to add a panel to. A telemetry-only landing is not a smaller answer chosen for convenience; it is the only one available here. ⛔ No cross-repo split needed, and none was taken.

### ⭐ And the static import is safer than the report claims

The one change carrying real risk was the **new static value import** into `serve.ts`. The dev justified it transitively (runtime already re-exports observability). I checked, and the simpler fact holds: **`@objectstack/observability` is already a direct `dependencies` entry of `packages/cli`** (`workspace:^`). The transitive path exists too (`runtime/src/index.ts:168`), but it isn't load-bearing. ⇒ No new failure mode, and no repeat of the boundary problem #12563 spent its whole measurement on.

### The fence held — verified in the diff, not in the prose

⛔ No enforcement, no membership view, no slot claim, no refusal. `multi-node-gate.ts` is **+19 lines of comments only**; nothing in the diff refuses anything. The verdict is read once at boot, held, and published. The cap stays advisory and every declared replica still joins.

⭐ **Three emissions are deliberately omitted rather than faked**, each with the false-reading it would produce written down: no `cluster_declared_nodes` when nothing was declared (`0` reads as "declared zero"); no `cluster_admitted_nodes` when the gate expressed no cap (any number invents a limit); nothing at all when the gate was never consulted. That is the honest-absence discipline applied without being asked for it — the brief asked for honest *naming*.

### ⭐ Two real defects the work found in itself

1. **Its own guard was vacuous, and its vacuity proof caught it.** The membership-claim sweep was first written with `\b` anchors — and `_` is a word character, so `\bactive\b` **does not match inside `cluster_active_nodes`**, precisely the rename the guard exists to reject. Every sweep would have reported green over the exact regression. Anchors are now `[^a-z0-9]`, and the vacuity proof asserting the sweep *rejects* `cluster_active_nodes` / `cluster_nodes_running` / `cluster_live_members` is what surfaced it. ⭐ A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard, and this one was caught by the test written to distrust it.
2. **`check:slot-lookup` went red and the fix improved safety rather than satisfying a ratchet.** The first draft resolved the metrics service into an `any`-typed variable (erasure 9 → 10). Typing it `MetricsRegistry` cleared the ratchet **and restored the argument check the erasure had switched off** — `counter(name, labels, value)` and `gauge(name, value, labels)` differ in argument order, so an `any` here would have let a swap compile and emit a label map where a number belongs. That is the ratchet doing the job it exists for.

### Verification

Suites: `@objectstack/cli` 41 across the four multi-node/observability files, `@objectstack/observability` 85, `@objectstack/service-cluster` 66. `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` confirms **both new test files are in the cli program**, so the green typecheck genuinely covers them. ⭐ Honest non-reading recorded rather than papered over: `observability` and `service-cluster` ship **no typecheck script**, so a `--filter typecheck` over them runs nothing — the dev says so and does not report a reading it did not take.

Gate union re-derived from the actual changed set: 25 families, 24 green; the one exception is `check-half-states` printing `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the token in the environment is not a valid GitHub credential` and exiting 3, read as **NOT MEASURED, not red** — correct, and its own text says nothing was swept.

Ablation, two legs, each proved on disk before its colour was read: verdict word pinned → 3/17 red on exactly the verdict rows (no `dist` involved, stated rather than assumed); the honest name renamed to a membership claim → 8/17 red including the sweep itself, with the package **rebuilt** because that consumption goes through `dist`. ⭐ And an honest detail worth keeping: the first `--absent` preflight reported a hit that was **not** a failed restore — the forbidden spelling legitimately appears in the new doc comment naming it as forbidden, and `tsup` preserves comments into `dist`. The mutated *value* was absent from source and dist alike. That is a lesson about marker choice, disclosed instead of quietly re-run.

Changeset: `minor` on `@objectstack/observability` and `@objectstack/cli` — correct, both gain public names.

### Next step

Clause-② `no` **holds**: no `packages/spec`, no new REST route, no new public client method; `SEMCONV` names are metric identifiers, not a contract accept/reject surface. Path face non-governed — **`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green** confirms it mechanically. CI at review time: **29 checks, 0 failures, converging.** ⇒ **Arming once every check is green** (ready + queue), pinned to `b7d45784`. ⛔ Not on the required subset.

### The flagged standing item — filed, not absorbed

The report flags that `@objectstack/runtime`'s `TEST_DEBT` records **227** while `tsc` now reports **226**, so one new error could land in that layer unreported until someone runs `--lower`. Pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to this card. ⛔ Correctly not fixed here. Filed as a `finding` for triage rather than left in a PR report where no queue can see it — a ratchet with slack is a small declared≠enforced gap, and "the tool prints its own repair command" is disclosure, not a mechanism.

## Landing window closed — MERGED, verified by content

PR #12720 landed on `origin/main`. Read out of the merged tree, ⛔ not off the merge event: `packages/observability/src/semconv.ts` carries `clusterDeclaredNodes`, and with it `clusterAdmittedNodes` / `clusterNodeCapVerdictsTotal`.

The fence held where it mattered: `multi-node-gate.ts` gained **comments only** — nothing in the landed diff refuses anything, counts peers, or turns the advisory cap into enforcement. ⛔ Option C's boundary (visibility, not enforcement) is intact on `main`.

`pm:dispatched` stripped, assignee released, read back. `service-cluster/**` released from this lane's hot-file serial queue.

⭐ The one thing worth carrying forward from this card: the surface is named for **what the operator declared** and **what the licence admits**, never for what is running — because this process has no cluster membership view at all. A future "helpful" rename to `cluster_nodes` or `cluster_active_nodes` would turn a true reading into a false one while every number stayed identical. There is now a test that rejects exactly that, and it only works because its own vacuity proof caught `\b` failing to match inside `cluster_active_nodes`.
